record.original_question: Do the prime numbers contain infinitely many patterns of the forms {m, m + [n^c], m + 2[n^c], ..., m + ℓ[n^c]} and {m, m + [n^c1], ..., m + [n^cℓ]} for given positive real exponents c, c1, ..., cℓ?

evidence.quote: Problem 30. Let ℓ ∈ N and c, c1, . . . , cℓ be positive real numbers. Show that the prime numbers contain patterns of the form {m, m + [n^c], m + 2[n^c], . . . , m + ℓ[n^c]} and {m, m + [n^c1], . . . , m + [n^cℓ]} for infinitely many n ∈ N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell$ be a positive integer and let $c, c_1, c_2, \dots, c_\ell$ be positive real numbers. For a real number $x$, denote by $[x]$ its integer part (floor). Prove or disprove each of the following statements:

(a) There exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which there is a positive integer $m$ such that all of
$$m,\; m + [n^c],\; m + 2[n^c],\; \dots,\; m + \ell\,[n^c]$$
are prime numbers.

(b) There exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which there is a positive integer $m$ such that all of
$$m,\; m + [n^{c_1}],\; m + [n^{c_2}],\; \dots,\; m + [n^{c_\ell}]$$
are prime numbers.

In other words, decide whether the primes contain infinitely many "Hardy-type" arithmetic progressions with common difference $[n^c]$ of length $\ell+1$, and infinitely many configurations whose gaps from a base point $m$ are prescribed by floors of arbitrary positive real powers of $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem appears to be open. The literature establishes that Piatetski-Shapiro primes (primes of the form $[n^c]$) exist infinitely often only in restricted ranges of $c$ (currently roughly $1 < c < 243/205$), and analogous results for primes in arithmetic progressions with Piatetski-Shapiro common difference are known only under similar restrictions. No result is known that handles arbitrary positive real exponents $c, c_1, \dots, c_\ell$ and arbitrary length $\ell$, so the full conjecture remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Piatetski-Shapiro prime number theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Infinitely many Piatetski-Shapiro primes are known for 1 < c < 1.1612...
status_evidence.claim: Existence of primes [n^c] is only established for restricted ranges of c, well short of 'all positive real c'.

status_evidence.title: Piatetski-Shapiro primes in arithmetic progressions
status_evidence.snippet: There exist infinitely many Piatetski-Shapiro primes in arithmetic progressions for 1<c<12/11.
status_evidence.claim: Pattern results combining primes and floors of powers are restricted to small ranges of c, supporting that the general problem is open.

status_evidence.title: Additive problems on ⌊p^c⌋
status_evidence.snippet: Recent additive problems involving ⌊n^c⌋ and primes continue to be active research with restrictions on c.
status_evidence.claim: The topic remains active and unresolved in full generality.
